description:
An `eval` domain for the shared relation registry — an open proposal koine has never recorded, and the first thing this tasklist owes is the record that it exists.

VERIFIED AGAINST THE TEXT (2026-09-12, before this tasklist was authored). `evaluated_by` and `verdict_of` appear in NO spec, registry table, schema or document in this repo — the only match anywhere is the roadmap row that records the ask. The registry holds three domain files today (`cinematography.tsv`, `media.tsv`, `social.tsv`) and 29 relation names across them and the core file.

THE ASK. Two `grounding-only` relations: `eval:evaluated_by` (`arg_roles` `artifact|evaluator`) and `eval:verdict_of` (`arg_roles` `verdict|artifact`). Both entity-to-entity, neither symmetric. They come from a producer whose evaluation verdicts currently project their LINEAGE and none of their READING: `derived_from` crosses today, and every measurement and finding is reported under `manifest.unprojected`, because ADR-0008 decision 1 and KGP §3.2 rule 1 forbid an adapter coining a relation — a relation name must be drawn from the shared registry, and the honest behaviour for a producer with no row is exactly the `unprojected` report it is filing.

WHY IT IS `feature` AND NOT `unblock`. Nothing is stopped. The producer works today and reports honestly; what it lacks is vocabulary, and what lands if the proposal is accepted is NET-NEW contract vocabulary that a consumer will read. The row's own harm statement is that an unanswered proposal makes an honest `unprojected` report look like a defect — which is a cost of silence, not a block. It is also the one row in this band with no deadline.

THE ASK IS NARROW ON PURPOSE, AND THE OBJECTION IS THE PRODUCER'S OWN. It carries NO SCORE. A row such as `eval:score(artifact, "7")` would merge two producers' sevens under KGP §3.3 convergence — regression rather than agreement — and the producer makes that objection itself rather than asking for the row. A decision that accepts the two and then quietly adds a third would be accepting a different proposal.

WHY IT DEPENDS ON THE `arg_types` COLUMN. Both relations are entity-to-entity, so all four argument positions are identifiers under KGP §3.2 rule 3 — and the whole point of INT-3's deadline is that the typing column lands BEFORE the registry gains wide production use, because a signature is immutable once published. Adding vocabulary first and typing it second is exactly the ordering the column exists to prevent.

WHAT IS OWED EITHER WAY: a recorded verdict. Accept or reject, and say which.

userStories.title: Record that the proposal exists, and decide it
userStories.description: koine has never received this in writing. The record comes first; the verdict follows from the registry's own governance rules.
acceptanceCriteria: The proposal is recorded in this repo for the first time: the two relations with their `arg_roles` (`artifact|evaluator`, `verdict|artifact`), their requested `grounding-only` tier, the fact that both are entity-to-entity and neither is symmetric, and what the asking producer does today instead (projects lineage via `derived_from` and reports the rest under `manifest.unprojected`).

The verdict is ACCEPT or REJECT and is stated as one, with its reasoning, measured against the registry's own governance — the shared-core-plus-namespaced-domain-extensions rule ratified 2026-07-17, `registry/README.md`'s standard for adding relations by PR, and ADR-0008 decision 1 (a producer's adapter coins no relation, which is why an unanswered proposal shows up as a consumer's honest `unprojected` report).

The no-score boundary is upheld and said to be upheld: no `eval:score`-shaped relation is added, and the reason is recorded — two producers' sevens would merge under KGP §3.3 convergence, which is regression rather than agreement. The producer raised that objection itself, and accepting a third row would be accepting a different proposal.
The asking producer is referred to BY ROLE, never by repository or product name — this repo is public and its rows are role-scoped and product-agnostic by design.

GATES: `node scripts/check-doc-integrity.mjs`, `node scripts/check-doc-links.mjs`, `node scripts/check-schemas.mjs`, `node scripts/check-registry.mjs`, `node scripts/check-tasklist-categories.mjs` and `bash scripts/check-roadmap-truth.sh` all green, with the observed output recorded.
userStories.notes: Recorded + decided in docs/reference/eval-relation-domain.md (new, informative; binds no clause, moves no version). Verified first-receipt before writing: `grep -rn 'evaluated_by|verdict_of'` over the tree matched only tasks/chief/1020-*.json and ROADMAP.md:412 — no spec, registry table, schema or doc. Verdict stated as one: ACCEPT both rows as a namespaced domain extension at grounding-only, typed id|id; measured against the 2026-07-17 shared-core-plus-namespaced-domain-extensions governance, registry/README.md's add-by-PR standard, and ADR-0008 decision 1. No-score boundary upheld with its reason (KGP §3.1/§3.3 convergence merges two producers' sevens, both prov records surviving) and its reconsideration trigger. Producer referred to by role only. GATES, observed: check-doc-integrity OK (every relative link resolves, all 3 status tables match their headers); check-doc-links 0 dead references, ratchet 0 dead vs 0 on main; check-schemas OK (9 schemas, 278 schema positions, 80 $refs, 3 fixtures); check-registry OK (29 relation names, unique across the core file and every domain file); check-tasklist-categories OK (10 tasklists categorized); check-roadmap-truth coverage OK (52 completed named), stale OK (42 merged checked, none shown as open), park OK. All six green. Carried in: ROADMAP.md's 1010-run-activity-identifier-grammar row was ⬜ while merged at 10a53c9 — check-roadmap-truth STALE was RED before this story and is green now.

userStories.title: If accepted, the domain lands the way every other domain did
userStories.description: A fourth domain file, typed, tiered, indexed and linked — or, on a reject, a recorded answer and no file.
acceptanceCriteria: If US-1's verdict is ACCEPT: `registry/relations/eval.tsv` exists with the exact column header every relation file carries — including the `arg_types` column this tasklist depends on — and both relations are typed at every argument position, tiered `grounding-only`, domain `eval`, and described in one line each.
`registry/README.md` names the new domain alongside `cine:`, `media:` and `soc:`, with the same one-line framing, so a project can tell which domains it may load.

`node scripts/check-registry.mjs` is green with the observed counts recorded — relation names unique across the core file and every domain file, column shape holding, every cross-file reference resolving (today: 29 relation names across four files).

The immutability rule is applied before the rows land, not after: a signature is immutable once published, so arity, argument order, symmetry and type are settled in this tasklist or the rows do not land at all.

If US-1's verdict is REJECT: no registry file is added, and the recorded answer states the condition under which the proposal would be reconsidered — the way `docs/reference/generative-audio-modalities.md` states a trigger rather than leaving a silence. This story is satisfied by either verdict provided US-1 reached one.
GATES: koine's six checks green, with observed output recorded.
